question: Which bill/act provided for the trial of British or European persons by Indians, and sought equality between British and Indian judges?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ilbert Bill of 1883**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Ilbert Bill** was introduced in **1883** by **Sir Courtenay Ilbert**, the Law Member of the Viceroy's Council during the tenure of **Lord Ripon**, the then Viceroy of India. 
• This bill proposed to allow **Indian judges** to preside over cases involving British and other European subjects in India, ensuring **judicial equality**. 
• The bill aimed to **abolish racial discrimination** in the Indian judicial system and was a major step toward **legal equality** between Indians and Europeans. 
• However, the bill faced **strong opposition** from the European community in India, who saw it as a threat to their privileged position. 
• Due to the backlash, the bill was **amended**, which led to a compromise. The amended version allowed European subjects to request a jury with at least half of its members being Europeans. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Background of the Ilbert Bill:** 
• Before the Ilbert Bill, the judicial system in India was **highly biased**, with British subjects being tried only by British judges. 
• The bill was part of Lord Ripon’s broader vision of **liberal reforms** and efforts to grant Indians more authority in governance. 
• **Impact of Opposition:** 
• The opposition to the Ilbert Bill highlighted the **deep-seated racial prejudices** among the European settlers in India. 
• The agitation against the bill reinforced the divide between Indians and Europeans, leading to a **greater nationalistic awakening** among Indians. 
• **Lord Ripon’s Legacy:** 
• Lord Ripon is remembered as the **“Father of Local Self-Government in India”** for his efforts to empower Indians in administrative roles. 
• Other notable reforms during his tenure include the **reduction of press restrictions** and the introduction of local self-governance. 
• **Significance of the Ilbert Bill:** 
• The Ilbert Bill controversy was a pivotal moment in Indian history, as it **exposed the discriminatory policies** of the British and inspired early nationalist movements. 
• It also encouraged Indians to **fight for equality and self-governance** through organized efforts. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Regulating Act of 1773:** 
• This act established the **Supreme Court of Judicature** in Calcutta and marked the beginning of the British judiciary in India. 
• It did not address the issue of judicial equality between Indians and Europeans. 
• **Pitt’s India Act of 1784:** 
• This act primarily dealt with the **administrative control** of the East India Company and did not involve judicial reforms. 
• **Indian Councils Act of 1892:** 
• This act was aimed at expanding the **legislative councils** and increasing Indian participation in governance but had no relevance to judicial matters.
